title: Tanzanian Nutritious Porridge
community: Enjoyed nationwide — particularly given to children, mothers, and the ill
author: Mama Salima
desc: Uji wa Lishe — Tanzanian nutritious porridge made from a blend of finger millet, sorghum, and maize flours with groundnut paste, sweetened with honey or sugar. The health porridge given to children, new mothers, and those recovering from illness — packed with nutrients.
longDesc: Uji wa Lishe (nutritious porridge) is Tanzania's answer to the question of how to pack the most nutrition into a single bowl. The combination of multiple grain flours with groundnut paste creates a porridge that is more nutritionally complete than any single grain alone. It is given to weaning children, nursing mothers, and anyone who needs nourishment.
steps: Mix all flours and groundnut paste with 1 cup cold water to a smooth slurry.
Bring remaining 3 cups water to a boil.
Pour slurry into boiling water, stirring constantly.
Cook over medium heat for 8—10 minutes until thick.
chefTips: The groundnut paste adds protein and healthy fats — do not omit.
Add honey off the heat to preserve its natural enzymes.
commonMistakes: Not making a slurry first — lumpy porridge.
Stopping stirring — sticks to the pot.
cookingScience: The combination of finger millet (high calcium and iron), sorghum (high antioxidants), maize (energy), and groundnuts (protein and fats) creates a nutritionally synergistic porridge where each ingredient contributes what the others lack.
sustainabilityTips: All grains grown in Tanzania — zero food miles.
reheating: Warm gently with a splash of water.
healthBenefits: Complete nutrition from multiple grain sources.
Groundnuts add protein and healthy fats.
culturalNote: Uji wa Lishe reflects Tanzania's traditional nutritional wisdom — the understanding that combining multiple foods produces something more nourishing than any single ingredient. It is the porridge that Tanzanian grandmothers make for their grandchildren and daughters.
